attacks.claim: The retry loop generates a fresh randomUUID() on every attempt, so the broker never sees the same client_order_id twice. If an attempt times out or returns 502/503/504 after the broker accepted the order, the retry submits a distinct second order and can double-fill. This breaks the agreed safe-retry constraint and contradicts the PR's own safety claim.

Changing Math.floor to Math.ceil rounds the buy quantity up past the available headroom, so sizeBuy can push a symbol above the maxNotional cap that sizing must never exceed (e.g., maxNotional 10000, price 33, lot 1 gives 304 shares = 10032). It also returns a full lot when headroom is less than one lot.
attacks.evidence:
const lots = headroom / price / lotSize;
  return Math.ceil(lots) * lotSize;

attacks.claim: The new sizing tests use only exact-multiple inputs, so they pass with the ceil cap violation present. No test covers non-integer headroom/price/lotSize, sub-lot headroom, or that a retry reuses the same client_order_id.
The retry logic in submit.ts has no tests at all (retryable 5xx, 4xx not retried, timeout retry, max attempts), yet it ships to a live-money order path before market open.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no test changes for src/router/submit.ts

attacks.claim: Timeout retry depends on the client throwing an error named exactly "TimeoutError" and honoring a new timeoutMs option, but no change to src/broker/client.ts is shown. If either assumption is wrong, timeouts are not retried or the 4000ms limit is not enforced, so the stated fix to the dropped-order problem doesn't work.
attacks.evidence: (err as Error).name === "TimeoutError"  and  { timeoutMs: 4000 }; ABSENT: change to src/broker/client.ts

attacks.claim: A live sizing behavior change and a retry change are bundled in one merge deploying right before market open, with no flag, staged rollout, or rollback plan, so a regression in either cannot be isolated or disabled quickly.
attacks.evidence: Also tidies the sizing helper so quantities are rounded to the broker's lot size before submit.  ABSENT: feature flag or rollback plan

attacks.claim: Observability is thin for a failure-prone path: only a warn log per retry, with no clientOrderId, no log/metric on final failure after exhausting retries, so operators cannot see dropped orders or reconcile a possibly-accepted order.
attacks.evidence: log.warn("order submit retry", { symbol: intent.symbol, attempt });  ABSENT: metric, alert, or final-failure log

attacks.claim: Worst-case retry window is about 13s with a fixed limit_price and no jitter, so late retries can submit at a stale price and synchronized retries can add load to a degraded broker. Transport errors such as connection resets are not retried.
